newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India may issue second Jan diesel tender - trader.
newsitem.headline: India may issue second Jan diesel tender - trader.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is likely to issue an additional tender to purchase diesel for delivery in January due to the closure of the two refineries after a crude pipeline explosion and a low award in its first tender, traders said on Thursday.
"There was news from India that IOC was going to issue a second tender but now the volume will be bigger," one trader said.
Traders said that IOC had already indicated that it was considering issuing a second tender as it had purchased only 255,000-tonnes in its first tender for January arrival cargoes.
Prior to the award, the market had initially estimated IOC requirement to be at least on par with its December purchase of 520,000-tonnes.

IOC now has a second reason to issue the tender as a result of the indefinite closure of the two refineries in the northeastern Indian state of Assam on Thursday after a pipeline burst following a bomb attack.

The Bongaigaon Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd, located in Assam has a annual capacity of 1.35 million tonnes, while the Barauni refinery located at Bihar state has a larger 3.3 million tonnes annual refining capacity.
"IOC is assessing the potential impact of the shutdown (to its requirement) and we should know something later today," one trader said.

Shipping sources said as the accident occurred in eastern India it would not compound IOC's port problems as the east coast ports of Madras and Haldia are relatively free unlike the west coast port of Kandla which is facing huge congestions due to the shutdown of two floating jetties since late October.
In the Singapore gas oil swaps market, December opened at $31.40/31.65 a barrel, unchnaged from Thursday. It traded to a high of $31.58 a barrel last night, one broker said.
